editorial:
Imagine waking up every day with a hole in your heart and a mind that won't stop playing tricks on you. You follow a photojournalist who is completely broken after his wife is killed. He isn't just sad; he is struggling to tell what is real and what is a dream. The vibe is very dark and tense, making you feel like someone is always watching from the shadows. It feels like a puzzle where the pieces don't quite fit, and you'll find yourself trying to solve the mystery right along with him as he hunts for the killer.

The acting is solid and makes you really feel the pain and confusion of the lead character. While the plot moves a bit slow in the middle, the payoff is totally worth it. If you love old-school mysteries that mess with your head, you need to see this. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture. If you are a fan of physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: At the very end, you find out that the main character has been lying to himself. The twist is that he actually killed his own wife during a mental breakdown, but his brain blocked it out to protect him. He wasn't hunting a stranger; he was chasing a ghost of his own making. The movie wraps up with him finally facing the truth, leaving him completely destroyed as the credits roll.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and dark mysteries.
